description: MECHANISM: a `repcount` READ nested inside a MALFORMED assignment target is an independent finding, reported ALONGSIDE `ol-not-a-place` (issue #1155). `first repcount = 5` is two separate mistakes — the target is not a place, AND the `repcount` in it reads a turn that does not exist — and fixing either leaves the other standing. This matches the checker's existing policy rather than inventing one: `first :undefined_name = 5` already reports `ol-not-a-place` and `ol-undefined-var` together. Only the target's ROOT is exempt from being read, which is what keeps the trap fixture `core-language/assignment/bare-place-invalid` (`repcount = 100`, where the word IS the root) reporting `ol-not-a-place` alone. An earlier draft suppressed the whole target subtree and cited `spec/execution-model.md:737` for it; that section governs which of two COMPETING diagnostics about one fault wins, not whether an unrelated finding elsewhere in the subtree may be suppressed. Measured falsification: suppressing the target subtree ONLY when its root is not a place kills this fixture and no other, so that is the wrong implementation this fixture walls. (A blunter mutation — never descending into a target at all — also kills `check/repcount-in-place-index-key`, so an earlier draft's claim that this was the sole wall for it, and that the rest of the corpus stayed green, was false; replayed against the very commit it named, that draft failed `repcount-in-place-index-key`.)
